summary: Steel Aermotor tower on Tussey Mountain, Huntingdon County: built 1933 at 80 feet, removed 1977; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Removed in 1977; no source describes what remains at the site.
facts.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Forests and Waters (ordered the 1933 towers); site in Logan State Forest district

events.note: Around 1910 a tree observation post 30 feet above the ground was set up on Tussey Mountain.
A 1912-13 state forestry report says an observatory station was erected on Tussey Mountain along the Pennsylvania Furnace road.
Three 80-foot towers were ordered in July 1933 and reported built by August; the Tussey one was among them.
A new aerial signal light was set on top of the tower, per a September 1938 newspaper item.
Registered September 16, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg.

notes_for_editor: Brief coordinates 40.6843, -77.9646 do not appear in any source read (firetower.org says none are available), so they were left unchanged. The link between the HawkCount 'former fire tower near Pennsylvania Furnace Rd' and this tower is inferred; the HawkCount page gives no date for that tower. Do not confuse this with the Little Flat tower in Rothrock State Forest on Tussey Mountain, which is a different lookout that appeared only in search results and was not read. No staffing or fire history appears in any source read.
